messages:
Sam Patel: quick ping — PR #2158 touches quant-routing path and adds a small TTL tweak for the prefix cache. can someone sanity-check perf/cost before we take it in this merge window? https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/2158 :eyes:
Alex Chen: on it. rough question — is TTL applied per-key or per-route?
Sam Patel: per-route, fallback to per-key if route has no override. default was 100ms, change sets route TTL to 150ms for long-seq workloads.
Marie Gomez: why the bump? are we seeing cold-kv misses causing extra decode?
Sam Patel: yep. on our 2k token internal eval, we saw a bunch of KV fetches at seq rollover. increasing TTL reduced re-hydration in the canary by ~18% tokens fetched from storage.
Jonah Lee: sounds plausible. do we have perf numbers vs cost? small latency regression maybe?
perf-bot: PR 2158 perf-check: p95 latency +5.8% (2k seq), p50 +1.2%, token-cost -12.3% for that trace. CI: all tests green.
Alex Chen: +5.8% p95 is notable. what's the absolute ms?
perf-bot: baseline p95= 110ms, new p95= 116.4ms (2k seq, n=120).
Marie Gomez: 6.4ms p95 increase for a 12% token-cost drop seems like a win for batch-heavy workloads, but for low-latency tiers we can't regress.
Sam Patel: agreed. I added a rollout flag to only enable TTL bump for 'throughput' tier routes and kept 'low-latency' routes at 100ms. code diff: ```yaml
routing:
  default_ttl_ms: 100
  overrides:
    throughput: 150
```
Alex Chen: that looks safe. can you add a doc blurb in the PR describing the tier mapping and the perf tradeoffs? reviewers skim that.
Sam Patel: done, pushed a follow-up commit with rationale + the perf CSV attached.
Jonah Lee: I'll take a look in ~30m. quick check: does this interact with KV eviction policy? we might be keeping items longer and bumping memory.
Sam Patel: good catch — I measured memory usage: ~+3% resident on canary. not huge but worth noting. added note.
Alex Chen: ok. if Jonah signs off, i'm fine with merging behind a feature-flag that defaults to off for low-latency customers.
Marie Gomez: +1 from me for throughput rollout, concerned about p95 for low-latency too.
Jonah Lee: reviewed and left 2 tiny comments (nits). overall LGTM. please squash and add a changelog line.
Sam Patel: thanks all. I'll squash and merge during the 4pm merge window and gate the flag. will post back after merge. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: merged PR 2158 into main (sha: b3f7a1c). canary rollout started.
Sam Patel: canary looks good so far — token cost down, p95 within 3% of baseline after minor tuning of batcher window. closing loop.
Alex Chen: awesome. thanks for the follow-up! :tada:
